title: Solve by completing the square

section.book: Bittinger, Beecher, Ellenbogen & Penna, College Algebra: Graphs and Models, 7e
section.title: Quadratic Equations, Functions, Zeros, and Models

sources: Bittinger 7e §3.2 Examples 5-6 (Video Notebook p. 75, missing from Don's PDF)

problem.prompt: Solve by completing the square: {tex:std} = 0. Find exact solutions.

steps.name: divide by a so the x-squared coefficient is 1
move the constant to the other side
add the square of half the x-coefficient to both sides
write the left side as a binomial squared
use the principle of square roots

mistakes.name: added (b/2)^2 to one side only
mistakes.message: Whatever you add on the left, add on the right too.

hints.step: divide by a so the x-squared coefficient is 1
hints.hint: If a is not 1, divide every term by a.
hints.why: The (b/2)^2 trick only works when x^2 has coefficient 1.

hints.step: move the constant to the other side
hints.hint: Move the constant term to the right side.
hints.why: Room is needed on the left for the number that completes the square.

hints.step: add the square of half the x-coefficient to both sides
hints.hint: Take half of the x-coefficient, square it, add it to both sides.
hints.why: It makes the left side a perfect-square trinomial.

hints.step: write the left side as a binomial squared
hints.hint: The left side is (x + half the x-coefficient)^2.

hints.step: use the principle of square roots
hints.hint: Take ± the square root of both sides.
hints.why: Principle of square roots: if X^2 = k, then X = ±sqrt(k).

hints.hint: Add the number next to x to both sides.
hints.why: That leaves x alone: the exact solutions.
